newsitem.title: GERMANY: Tchibo says it formally applied to buy Eduscho.
newsitem.headline: Tchibo says it formally applied to buy Eduscho.

text.p: Germany's Tchibo Holding AG said it had submitted a formal application for the purchase of competing coffee roaster Eduscho to the federal cartel office in Berlin on Wednesday.
"The authority now has the papers," a spokesman said.
Tchibo and Eduscho announced the planned transaction a week ago. The cartel office has expressed some irritation about not having been swiftly informed about the merger plans.
The office has up to four months to study joint sales values, the future position of the companies and the competitive environment.
Under the proposed purchase, Tchibo would buy Eduscho GmbH & Co Kg, effective January 1, 1997.

The two companies would be battling with Kraft Jacobs Suchard for market leadership. Kraft Jacobs Suchard holds 30.7 percent of roasted coffee sales volumes in Germany while Eduscho has 11 percent and Tchibo a good 19 percent of the market.

The two premium roasters are unique in that they sell their coffee in tied outlets along with consumer goods -- unlike their competitors, who sell to wholesale and grocery chains, where they have a limited role in setting final retail prices.
